correctness.rationale: Affine Boolean truth tables map under s=1−2y and orthogonal Walsh H to unit ℓ1-ball: P_m={1/2·1−1/2 H z:||z||_1≤1}, and ||y−(1−H z)/2||²=(n/4)||w−z||². KKT projection gives exact signed soft-threshold z and distance n/4∑min(|w_a|,τ)², plus active support simplex face (|A|−1). For binary y Parseval ||w||₂=1, hence ||w||₁≤√n; comparison with radial w/L gives max distance≤(√n−1)/2. Even m has explicit bent quadratic with flat |w|=1/√n attaining bound; equality in Cauchy–Schwarz iff bent, with all n active coordinates and facet projection. Distinct bent vertex residuals force strict variance for nonvertex combinations. Odd m cannot attain because integer Walsh sums cannot equal irrational 2^(m/2). Independent full enumeration m2,m3,m4 matches max squares .25,.5625,2.25 and bent counts 8,0,896; all m claim analytic.

value.rationale: The complete exact Euclidean convex decoder for arbitrary real received vectors and minimal projection-face structure on the canonical RM(1,m) codeword polytope is a natural useful metric/geometric invariant, and the sharp even-dimensional Hausdorff and bent-only farthest-locus add nontrivial global classification. Known Walsh crosspolytope, soft-threshold and bent facts are credited, not independently sold as discoveries. Unlike generic single-ingredient reformulation, the all-input metric decoding rule and global extremal proof address a concrete natural object and a different objective than prior random-access coding.

limitations: Exact Hausdorff sharp formula only for even m≥2; odd m strict upper bound with no exact maximum claimed. Arbitrary real inputs admit full projection formula for every m≥2.
Known soft-threshold and bent Walsh-flatness precede audited result; no independent human certification and equivalent obscure Euclidean formulation may exist.
